1	/*
2	ANS Complete EBNF Grammar
3	Sebesta-style notation for the implemented C-like ANS subset.
4	
5	Conventions:
6	  <nonterminal> ::= production
7	  "terminal" means exact source text
8	  { X } means zero or more repetitions of X
9	  [ X ] means optional X
10	  | means alternative
11	  EOF means end of file
12	
13	Important lexer convention:
14	  ANS uses contextual chemistry words. Lowercase words are first tokenized
15	  as IDENTIFIER-like words. The parser interprets words such as element,
16	  compound, reaction, formula, reactants, products, balanced, exothermic,
17	  and endothermic as special words only in grammar positions where they
18	  have special meaning. This allows function parameters such as reaction,
19	  mol, and compound in:
20	
21	      function compute_yield(reaction, mol, compound) { ... };
22	*/
23	
24	/* ============================================================
25	   1. Program Structure
26	   ============================================================ */
27	
28	<program> ::= { <top_level_statement> } EOF
29	
30	<top_level_statement> ::= <element_declaration> ";"
31	                        | <compound_declaration> ";"
32	                        | <reaction_declaration> ";"
33	                        | <function_declaration> ";"
34	                        | <variable_declaration> ";"
35	                        | <assignment_statement> ";"
36	                        | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
37	                        | <print_statement> ";"
38	                        | <expression_statement> ";"
39	                        | <if_statement>
40	
41	/* ============================================================
42	   2. General Statements and Blocks
43	   ============================================================ */
44	
45	<block> ::= "{" { <statement> } "}"
46	
47	<statement> ::= <variable_declaration> ";"
48	              | <assignment_statement> ";"
49	              | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
50	              | <return_statement> ";"
51	              | <print_statement> ";"
52	              | <expression_statement> ";"
53	              | <for_statement>
54	              | <if_statement>
55	
56	<variable_declaration> ::= "let" <identifier> "=" <expression>
57	
58	<assignment_statement> ::= <assignable> "=" <expression>
59	
60	<augmented_assignment_statement> ::= <assignable> <augmented_assignment_operator> <expression>
61	
62	<augmented_assignment_operator> ::= "+="
63	                                  | "-="
64	                                  | "*="
65	                                  | "/="
66	
67	<return_statement> ::= "return" [ <expression> ]
68	
69	<print_statement> ::= "print" <expression>
70	
71	<expression_statement> ::= <expression>
72	
73	/* ============================================================
74	   3. Function Declarations
75	   ============================================================ */
76	
77	<function_declaration> ::= "function" <identifier> "(" [ <parameter_list> ] ")" <block>
78	
79	<parameter_list> ::= <identifier> { "," <identifier> }
80	
81	/* Ambiguity resolution:
82	   Words such as reaction, mol, and compound are parsed as <identifier>
83	   in <parameter_list>. They are not treated as declaration keywords here.
84	*/
85	
86	/* ============================================================
87	   4. For Loops
88	   ============================================================ */
89	
90	<for_statement> ::= "for" "(" "let" <identifier> "in" <expression> ")" <block>
91	
92	/* Example:
93	   for (let element in formula) {
94	       mass += element.atomic_mass * formula[element];
95	   }
96	*/
97	
98	/* ============================================================
99	   5. If / Elif / Else Statements
100	   ============================================================ */
101	
102	<if_statement> ::= "if" <expression> <block> { <elif_clause> } [ <else_clause> ]
103	
104	<elif_clause> ::= "elif" <expression> <block>
105	
106	<else_clause> ::= "else" <block>
107	
108	/* Ambiguity resolution: dangling else
109	   The optional <else_clause> belongs to the nearest preceding <if_statement>
110	   in this grammar. Because every branch body is a braced <block>, there is
111	   no ambiguous unbraced statement such as:
112	       if a if b s else t
113	   Therefore the classic dangling-else ambiguity is avoided.
114	*/
115	
116	/* ============================================================
117	   6. Element Declarations
118	   ============================================================ */
119	
120	<element_declaration> ::= "element" <element_symbol> "{" <element_field_list> "}"
121	
122	<element_symbol> ::= <formula_literal>
123	
124	<element_field_list> ::= <element_field> { "," <element_field> } [ "," ]
125	
126	<element_field> ::= "atomic_mass" "=" <number_literal>
127	                  | "valence" "=" <number_literal>
128	                  | "symbol" "=" <string_literal>
129	
130	/* Semantic requirements:
131	   - <element_symbol> must be a single valid periodic-table symbol, such as H.
132	   - The element body must contain atomic_mass, valence, and symbol exactly once.
133	   - Duplicate or missing fields are semantic errors, not syntax errors.
134	
135	   Ambiguity resolution:
136	   H is lexically a <formula_literal>, but after "element" it is interpreted
137	   as an element symbol declaration.
138	*/
139	
140	/* ============================================================
141	   7. Compound Declarations
142	   ============================================================ */
143	
144	<compound_declaration> ::= "compound" <identifier> "{" <compound_field_list> "}"
145	
146	<compound_field_list> ::= <compound_field> { "," <compound_field> } [ "," ]
147	
148	<compound_field> ::= "formula" "=" <formula_literal>
149	                   | "name" "=" <string_literal>
150	
151	/* Semantic requirements:
152	   - The compound body must contain formula and name exactly once.
153	   - Every element symbol inside <formula_literal> must refer to a declared
154	     or built-in element.
155	*/
156	
157	/* ============================================================
158	   8. Reaction Declarations
159	   ============================================================ */
160	
161	<reaction_declaration> ::= "reaction" <identifier> "{" <reaction_field_list> "}"
162	
163	<reaction_field_list> ::= <reaction_field> { "," <reaction_field> } [ "," ]
164	
165	<reaction_field> ::= "reactants" "=" <reaction_expression>
166	                   | "products" "=" <reaction_expression>
167	                   | "check" "=" <balance_check>
168	                   | "energy" "=" <energy_expression>
169	
170	<balance_check> ::= "balanced"
171	
172	<energy_expression> ::= <energy_kind> <quantity_literal>
173	
174	<energy_kind> ::= "exothermic"
175	                | "endothermic"
176	
177	/* Semantic requirements:
178	   - The reaction body must contain reactants, products, check, and energy
179	     exactly once.
180	   - If check = balanced appears, the semantic checker verifies equal atom
181	     counts on both sides.
182	   - exothermic 890.3 kJ/mol is stored internally as a negative energy change.
183	   - endothermic 890.3 kJ/mol is stored internally as a positive energy change.
184	*/
185	
186	/* ============================================================
187	   9. Reaction Expressions
188	   ============================================================ */
189	
190	<reaction_expression> ::= <reaction_term> { "+" <reaction_term> }
191	
192	<reaction_term> ::= <species_ref>
193	                  | <coefficient> "*" <species_ref>
194	
195	<coefficient> ::= <number_literal>
196	
197	<species_ref> ::= <formula_literal>
198	                | <identifier>
199	
200	/* Examples accepted:
201	   CH4 + 2*O2
202	   CO2 + 2*H2O
203	   methane + 2*oxygen
204	   co2 + 2*water
205	
206	   Ambiguity resolution:
207	   <reaction_expression> is separate from <expression>. In reactions, +
208	   separates chemical species, and * attaches a coefficient to one species.
209	   Therefore CH4 + 2*O2 parses as CH4 + (2*O2), not as (CH4 + 2) * O2.
210	
211	   ANS requires 2*O2 instead of 2O2 to avoid ambiguity between a
212	   stoichiometric coefficient and a formula subscript.
213	*/
214	
215	/* ============================================================
216	   10. Expressions
217	   ============================================================ */
218	
219	<expression> ::= <comparison_expression>
220	
221	<comparison_expression> ::= <additive_expression> [ <comparison_operator> <additive_expression> ]
222	
223	<comparison_operator> ::= "=="
224	                        | "!="
225	                        | ">="
226	                        | "<="
227	                        | ">"
228	                        | "<"
229	
230	<additive_expression> ::= <multiplicative_expression>
231	                          { ("+" | "-") <multiplicative_expression> }
232	
233	<multiplicative_expression> ::= <unary_expression>
234	                                { ("*" | "/") <unary_expression> }
235	
236	<unary_expression> ::= [ "-" ] <postfix_expression>
237	
238	<postfix_expression> ::= <primary_expression> { <postfix_operator> }
239	
240	<postfix_operator> ::= "." <identifier>
241	                     | "[" <expression> "]"
242	                     | "(" [ <argument_list> ] ")"
243	
244	<primary_expression> ::= <number_or_quantity_literal>
245	                       | <string_literal>
246	                       | <char_literal>
247	                       | <list_literal>
248	                       | <formula_literal>
249	                       | <identifier>
250	                       | "(" <expression> ")"
251	
252	<argument_list> ::= <expression> { "," <expression> }
253	
254	<number_or_quantity_literal> ::= <number_literal> [ <unit_literal> ]
255	
256	<quantity_literal> ::= <number_literal> <unit_literal>
257	
258	<list_literal> ::= "[" [ <argument_list> ] "]"
259	
260	/* Examples accepted:
261	   20
262	   21.2
263	   5.0 mol
264	   890.3 kJ/mol
265	   'H'
266	   [1, "two", 3.45, water, methane.formula, H]
267	   reaction.products
268	   reactants[compound].mol
269	   element.atomic_mass * formula[element]
270	   molar_mass(water)
271	   compute_yield(combustion, 5.0 mol, CH4)
272	
273	   Ambiguity resolution: operator precedence
274	   Precedence is encoded by the rule hierarchy:
275	     1. primary expressions and parenthesized expressions
276	     2. postfix operations: call, indexing, property access
277	     3. unary -
278	     4. * and /
279	     5. + and -
280	     6. comparison operators
281	
282	   Thus a + b * c parses as a + (b * c), and
283	   element.atomic_mass * formula[element] parses as
284	   (element.atomic_mass) * (formula[element]).
285	
286	   Binary +, -, *, and / are left-associative because they repeat from left
287	   to right in their own grammar level.
288	*/
289	
290	/* ============================================================
291	   11. Assignable Expressions
292	   ============================================================ */
293	
294	<assignable> ::= <identifier> { <assignable_postfix> }
295	
296	<assignable_postfix> ::= "." <identifier>
297	                       | "[" <expression> "]"
298	
299	/* Examples accepted:
300	   mass
301	   reaction.products
302	   reactants[compound].mol
303	   formula[element]
304	
305	   Ambiguity resolution:
306	   Function-call syntax is not allowed in <assignable>, so f(x) = 3 is not
307	   valid in ANS.
308	*/
309	
310	/* ============================================================
311	   12. Lexical Nonterminals
312	   ============================================================ */
313	
314	<identifier> ::= IDENTIFIER
315	
316	<number_literal> ::= NUMBER_LITERAL
317	
318	<string_literal> ::= STRING_LITERAL
319	
320	<char_literal> ::= CHAR_LITERAL
321	
322	<formula_literal> ::= FORMULA_LITERAL
323	
324	<unit_literal> ::= UNIT_LITERAL
325	
326	/* Lexer patterns:
327	
328	   IDENTIFIER:
329	       [a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
330	
331	   NUMBER_LITERAL:
332	       (?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?
333	
334	   STRING_LITERAL:
335	       "(?:[^"\\\r\n]|\\["\\nrt])*"
336	
337	   CHAR_LITERAL:
338	       '(?:[^'\\\r\n]|\\['\\nrt])'
339	
340	   FORMULA_LITERAL:
341	       (?:[A-Z][a-z]?(?:[1-9][0-9]*)?)+
342	
343	   UNIT_LITERAL:
344	       (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:kg/mol|g/mol|kJ/mol|mol|kg|g|kJ)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])
345	
346	   OPERATOR:
347	       ==|!=|>=|<=|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|=|[+\-*/><]
348	
349	   SEPARATOR:
350	       [{}()\[\],;.]
351	
352	   COMMENT:
353	       #[^\r\n]*
354	
355	   WHITESPACE:
356	       [ \t\f\r\n]+
357	*/
358	
359	/* ============================================================
360	   13. Contextual Keyword and Unit Resolution
361	   ============================================================ */
362	
363	/* Hard reserved words in the implemented subset:
364	     let, function, return, for, in, if, elif, else, print
365	
366	   Contextual declaration/chemistry words:
367	     element, compound, reaction, atomic_mass, valence, symbol, formula,
368	     name, reactants, products, check, balanced, energy, exothermic,
369	     endothermic
370	
371	   Contextual unit words:
372	     mol, g, kg, g/mol, kg/mol, kJ, kJ/mol
373	
374	   Resolution rules:
375	   - At the start of a declaration, element, compound, and reaction are
376	     parsed as declaration keywords.
377	   - Inside declaration bodies, atomic_mass, valence, symbol, formula, name,
378	     reactants, products, check, and energy are parsed as field names.
379	   - In parameter, expression, and property positions, the same lowercase words
380	     may be parsed as identifiers.
381	   - A unit literal is recognized as part of a quantity only when it follows
382	     a number, as in 5.0 mol or 890.3 kJ/mol.
383	   - Elsewhere, mol may be an identifier, as in a function parameter named mol.
384	*/
385	
386	/* ============================================================
387	   14. Ambiguity Summary
388	   ============================================================ */
389	
390	/*
391	1. Operator precedence:
392	   Resolved by separate comparison, additive, multiplicative, unary, postfix,
393	   and primary expression levels.
394	
395	2. Reaction precedence:
396	   Resolved by a separate <reaction_expression> grammar.
397	
398	3. Stoichiometric coefficient ambiguity:
399	   Resolved by requiring 2*O2 instead of 2O2.
400	
401	4. Formula versus identifier ambiguity:
402	   Reduced lexically because identifiers start lowercase or _, while formulas
403	   start uppercase. water is an identifier; H2O is a formula literal.
404	
405	5. Compound-name species versus formula species:
406	   Resolved by <species_ref>, which allows either a formula literal or a
407	   compound identifier inside reaction expressions.
408	
409	6. Keyword versus identifier ambiguity:
410	   Resolved with contextual keywords. This allows reaction and compound to be
411	   used as function parameter names.
412	
413	7. Unit versus identifier ambiguity:
414	   Resolved contextually. mol is a unit after a number, but an identifier
415	   elsewhere.
416	
417	8. Dangling else:
418	   Avoided by requiring every if, elif, and else branch to use a braced block;
419	   the optional else attaches to the nearest preceding if statement.
420	
421	9. Function call versus assignable expression:
422	   Function calls are valid expressions but not valid assignment targets.
423	
424	10. Duplicate declaration fields:
425	    Field duplication and missing required fields are semantic errors.
426	*/
427

   11. Assignable Expressions
   ============================================================ */

(*
ANS Complete EBNF Grammar
Sebesta-style notation for the implemented C-like ANS subset.

Conventions:
  <nonterminal> → production
  terminal      means exact source text (shown in lowercase or quoted)
  { X }         means zero or more repetitions of X
  [ X ]         means optional X
  ( X | Y )     means one of the alternatives X or Y
  |             separates top-level alternatives in a rule
  EOF           means end of file

Important lexer convention:
  ANS uses contextual chemistry words. Lowercase words are first tokenized
  as IDENTIFIER-like words. The parser interprets words such as element,
  compound, reaction, formula, reactants, products, balanced, exothermic,
  and endothermic as special words only in grammar positions where they
  have special meaning. This allows function parameters such as reaction,
  mol, and compound in:

      function compute_yield(reaction, mol, compound) { ... };
*)

(* ============================================================
   1. Program Structure
   ============================================================ *)

<program> → { <top_level_statement> } EOF

<top_level_statement> → <element_declaration> ";"
                      | <compound_declaration> ";"
                      | <reaction_declaration> ";"
                      | <function_declaration> ";"
                      | <variable_declaration> ";"
                      | <assignment_statement> ";"
                      | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
                      | <print_statement> ";"
                      | <expression_statement> ";"
                      | <if_statement>

(* ============================================================
   2. General Statements and Blocks
   ============================================================ *)

<block> → "{" { <statement> } "}"

<statement> → <variable_declaration> ";"
            | <assignment_statement> ";"
            | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
            | <return_statement> ";"
            | <print_statement> ";"
            | <expression_statement> ";"
            | <for_statement>
            | <if_statement>

<variable_declaration> → "let" <identifier> "=" <expression>

<assignment_statement> → <assignable> "=" <expression>

<augmented_assignment_statement> → <assignable> <augmented_assignment_operator> <expression>

<augmented_assignment_operator> → "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/="

<return_statement> → "return" [ <expression> ]

<print_statement> → "print" <expression>

<expression_statement> → <expression>

(* ============================================================
   3. Function Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<function_declaration> → "function" <identifier> "(" [ <parameter_list> ] ")" <block>

<parameter_list> → <identifier> { "," <identifier> }

(* Words such as reaction, mol, and compound are parsed as <identifier>
   in <parameter_list>. They are not treated as declaration keywords here. *)

(* ============================================================
   4. For Loops
   ============================================================ *)

<for_statement> → "for" "(" "let" <identifier> "in" <expression> ")" <block>

(* Example:
   for (let element in formula) {
       mass += element.atomic_mass * formula[element];
   }
*)

(* ============================================================
   5. If / Elif / Else Statements
   ============================================================ *)

<if_statement> → "if" <expression> <block> { <elif_clause> } [ <else_clause> ]

<elif_clause> → "elif" <expression> <block>

<else_clause> → "else" <block>

(* Dangling-else resolution:
   Every branch body is a braced <block>, so the classic unbraced ambiguity
       if a if b s else t
   cannot arise. The optional <else_clause> belongs to the nearest preceding
   <if_statement>. *)

(* ============================================================
   6. Element Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<element_declaration> → "element" <element_symbol> "{" <element_field_list> "}"

<element_symbol> → <formula_literal>

<element_field_list> → <element_field> { "," <element_field> } [ "," ]

<element_field> → "atomic_mass" "=" <number_literal>
                | "valence"     "=" <number_literal>
                | "symbol"      "=" <string_literal>

(* Semantic requirements:
   - <element_symbol> must be a single valid periodic-table symbol (e.g., H).
   - The element body must contain atomic_mass, valence, and symbol exactly once.
   - Duplicate or missing fields are semantic errors, not syntax errors.
   H is lexically a <formula_literal>; after "element" it is an element symbol. *)

(* ============================================================
   7. Compound Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<compound_declaration> → "compound" <identifier> "{" <compound_field_list> "}"

<compound_field_list> → <compound_field> { "," <compound_field> } [ "," ]

<compound_field> → "formula" "=" <formula_literal>
                 | "name"    "=" <string_literal>

(* Semantic requirements:
   - The compound body must contain formula and name exactly once.
   - Every element symbol inside <formula_literal> must refer to a declared
     or built-in element. *)

(* ============================================================
   8. Reaction Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<reaction_declaration> → "reaction" <identifier> "{" <reaction_field_list> "}"

<reaction_field_list> → <reaction_field> { "," <reaction_field> } [ "," ]

<reaction_field> → "reactants" "=" <reaction_expression>
                 | "products"  "=" <reaction_expression>
                 | "check"     "=" <balance_check>
                 | "energy"    "=" <energy_expression>

<balance_check> → "balanced"

<energy_expression> → <energy_kind> <quantity_literal>

<energy_kind> → "exothermic" | "endothermic"

(* Semantic requirements:
   - The reaction body must contain reactants, products, check, and energy
     exactly once.
   - If check = balanced appears, the semantic checker verifies equal atom
     counts on both sides.
   - exothermic stores a negative delta-energy; endothermic stores positive. *)

(* ============================================================
   9. Reaction Expressions
   ============================================================ *)

<reaction_expression> → <reaction_term> { "+" <reaction_term> }

<reaction_term> → <species_ref>
                | <coefficient> "*" <species_ref>

<coefficient> → <number_literal>

<species_ref> → <formula_literal> | <identifier>

(* Examples accepted:
       CH4 + 2*O2        CO2 + 2*H2O
       methane + 2*oxygen    co2 + 2*water

   In reaction context + separates species and * attaches a coefficient, so
   CH4 + 2*O2 parses as CH4 + (2*O2), not (CH4 + 2) * O2.
   ANS requires 2*O2 rather than 2O2 to avoid ambiguity with formula subscripts. *)

(* ============================================================
   10. Expressions
   ============================================================ *)

<expression> → <comparison_expression>

<comparison_expression> → <additive_expression>
                          [ ( "==" | "!=" | ">=" | "<=" | ">" | "<" )
                            <additive_expression> ]

<additive_expression> → <multiplicative_expression>
                        { ( "+" | "-" ) <multiplicative_expression> }

<multiplicative_expression> → <unary_expression>
                               { ( "*" | "/" ) <unary_expression> }

<unary_expression> → [ "-" ] <postfix_expression>

<postfix_expression> → <primary_expression> { <postfix_operator> }

<postfix_operator> → "." <identifier>
                   | "[" <expression> "]"
                   | "(" [ <argument_list> ] ")"

<primary_expression> → <number_or_quantity_literal>
                     | <string_literal>
                     | <char_literal>
                     | <list_literal>
                     | <formula_literal>
                     | <identifier>
                     | "(" <expression> ")"

<argument_list> → <expression> { "," <expression> }

<number_or_quantity_literal> → <number_literal> [ <unit_literal> ]

<quantity_literal> → <number_literal> <unit_literal>

<list_literal> → "[" [ <argument_list> ] "]"

(* Operator precedence (lowest to highest):
   1. comparison:    == != >= <= > <
   2. additive:      + -
   3. multiplicative: * /
   4. unary:         -
   5. postfix:       call ( ), index [ ], property .
   6. primary:       literals, identifiers, ( <expression> )
   Binary +, -, *, / are left-associative (left-to-right repetition in grammar). *)

(* ============================================================
   11. Assignable Expressions
   ============================================================ *)

<assignable> → <identifier> { <assignable_postfix> }

<assignable_postfix> → "." <identifier>
                     | "[" <expression> "]"

(* Function-call syntax is excluded from <assignable>, so f(x) = 3 is invalid. *)

(* ============================================================
   12. Lexical Nonterminals
   ============================================================ *)

<identifier>     → IDENTIFIER
<number_literal> → NUMBER_LITERAL
<string_literal> → STRING_LITERAL
<char_literal>   → CHAR_LITERAL
<formula_literal> → FORMULA_LITERAL
<unit_literal>   → UNIT_LITERAL

(* Lexer patterns:

   IDENTIFIER:
       [a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*

   NUMBER_LITERAL:
       (?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?

   STRING_LITERAL:
       "(?:[^"\\\r\n]|\\["\\nrt])*"

   CHAR_LITERAL:
       '(?:[^'\\\r\n]|\\['\\nrt])'

   FORMULA_LITERAL:
       (?:[A-Z][a-z]?(?:[1-9][0-9]*)?)+

   UNIT_LITERAL:
       (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:kg/mol|g/mol|kJ/mol|mol|kg|g|kJ)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])

   OPERATOR:
       ==|!=|>=|<=|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|=|[+\-*/><]

   SEPARATOR:
       [{}()\[\],;.]

   COMMENT:
       #[^\r\n]*

   WHITESPACE:
       [ \t\f\r\n]+
*)

(* ============================================================
   13. Contextual Keyword and Unit Resolution
   ============================================================ *)

(* Hard reserved words:
     let  function  return  for  in  if  elif  else  print

   Contextual declaration/chemistry words:
     element  compound  reaction  atomic_mass  valence  symbol  formula
     name  reactants  products  check  balanced  energy  exothermic  endothermic

   Contextual unit words:
     mol  g  kg  g/mol  kg/mol  kJ  kJ/mol

   Resolution rules:
   - At declaration start, element/compound/reaction are declaration keywords.
   - Inside declaration bodies, field-name words are field identifiers.
   - In parameter, expression, and property positions the same words are identifiers.
   - A unit literal is recognised only when it directly follows a number (5.0 mol).
   - Elsewhere mol and similar words are plain identifiers. *)

(* ============================================================
   14. Ambiguity Summary
   ============================================================ *)

(*
1. Operator precedence:
   Resolved by separate comparison, additive, multiplicative, unary, postfix,
   and primary expression levels.

2. Reaction precedence:
   Resolved by a separate <reaction_expression> grammar.

3. Stoichiometric coefficient ambiguity:
   Resolved by requiring 2*O2 instead of 2O2.

4. Formula versus identifier ambiguity:
   Identifiers start with a lowercase letter or _; formula literals start with
   an uppercase letter. water is an identifier; H2O is a formula literal.

5. Compound-name species versus formula species:
   Resolved by <species_ref>, which accepts either form inside reactions.

6. Keyword versus identifier ambiguity:
   Resolved with contextual keywords, permitting reaction and compound as
   function parameter names.

7. Unit versus identifier ambiguity:
   Resolved contextually: mol is a unit after a number, an identifier elsewhere.

8. Dangling else:
   Avoided by requiring braced <block> bodies; else attaches to the nearest if.

9. Function call versus assignable expression:
   Function calls are valid expressions but not valid assignment targets.

10. Duplicate declaration fields:
    Field duplication and missing required fields are semantic errors.
*)

(*
ANS Complete EBNF Grammar
Sebesta-style notation for the implemented C-like ANS subset.

Conventions:
  <nonterminal> → production
  terminal      means exact source text (shown in lowercase or quoted)
  { X }         means zero or more repetitions of X
  [ X ]         means optional X
  ( X | Y )     means one of the alternatives X or Y
  |             separates top-level alternatives in a rule
  EOF           means end of file

Important lexer convention:
  ANS uses contextual chemistry words. Lowercase words are first tokenized
  as IDENTIFIER-like words. The parser interprets words such as element,
  compound, reaction, formula, reactants, products, balanced, exothermic,
  and endothermic as special words only in grammar positions where they
  have special meaning. This allows typed parameters such as:

      function compute_yield(reaction r, compound c) { ... };
      function molar_mass(compound c) { ... };
*)

(* ============================================================
   1. Program Structure
   ============================================================ *)

<program> → { <top_level_statement> } EOF

<top_level_statement> → <import_statement> ";"
                      | <element_declaration> ";"
                      | <compound_declaration> ";"
                      | <reaction_declaration> ";"
                      | <function_declaration> ";"
                      | <variable_declaration> ";"
                      | <assignment_statement> ";"
                      | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
                      | <print_statement> ";"
                      | <expression_statement> ";"
                      | <if_statement>

(* ============================================================
   2. Import Statements
   ============================================================ *)

<import_statement> → "import" <identifier>

(* Examples accepted:
       import std

   Semantic requirement: the named module must exist in the ANS standard library
   or the local module path. Import resolution is a semantic phase concern. *)

(* ============================================================
   3. General Statements and Blocks
   ============================================================ *)

<block> → "{" { <statement> } "}"

<statement> → <variable_declaration> ";"
            | <assignment_statement> ";"
            | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
            | <return_statement> ";"
            | <print_statement> ";"
            | <expression_statement> ";"
            | <for_statement>
            | <if_statement>

<variable_declaration> → "let" <identifier> "=" <expression>

<assignment_statement> → <assignable> "=" <expression>

<augmented_assignment_statement> → <assignable> <augmented_assignment_operator> <expression>

<augmented_assignment_operator> → "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/="

<return_statement> → "return" [ <expression> ]

<print_statement> → "print" <expression>

<expression_statement> → <expression>

(* ============================================================
   4. Function Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<function_declaration> → "function" <identifier> "(" [ <parameter_list> ] ")" <block>

<parameter_list> → <parameter> { "," <parameter> }

<parameter> → [ <type_name> ] <identifier>

<type_name> → "element" | "compound" | "reaction"

(* Typed parameters allow the type-checker to verify that the correct kind of
   value is passed at call sites. The type annotation is optional; untyped
   parameters accept any value. Examples:
       reaction r    compound c    element e    mol (untyped)

   Ambiguity resolution:
   element, compound, and reaction are parsed as <type_name> only when they
   immediately precede an <identifier> inside a <parameter_list>. Elsewhere
   these words may still appear as identifiers. *)

(* ============================================================
   5. For Loops
   ============================================================ *)

<for_statement> → "for" "(" "let" <identifier> "in" <expression> ")" <block>

(* Example:
   for (let element in formula) {
       mass += element.atomic_mass * formula[element];
   }
*)

(* ============================================================
   6. If / Elif / Else Statements
   ============================================================ *)

<if_statement> → "if" "(" <expression> ")" <block>
                 { <elif_clause> } [ <else_clause> ]

<elif_clause> → "elif" "(" <expression> ")" <block>

<else_clause> → "else" <block>

(* Conditions are always wrapped in parentheses, matching the for-loop style.

   Dangling-else resolution:
   Every branch body is a braced <block>, so the classic unbraced ambiguity
       if a if b s else t
   cannot arise. The optional <else_clause> belongs to the nearest preceding
   <if_statement>. *)

(* ============================================================
   7. Element Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<element_declaration> → "element" <element_symbol> "{" <element_field_list> "}"

<element_symbol> → <formula_literal>

<element_field_list> → <element_field> { "," <element_field> } [ "," ]

<element_field> → "atomic_mass" "=" <number_literal>
                | "valence"     "=" <number_literal>
                | "symbol"      "=" <string_literal>

(* Semantic requirements:
   - <element_symbol> must be a single valid periodic-table symbol (e.g., H).
   - The element body must contain atomic_mass, valence, and symbol exactly once.
   - Duplicate or missing fields are semantic errors, not syntax errors.
   H is lexically a <formula_literal>; after "element" it is an element symbol. *)

(* ============================================================
   8. Compound Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<compound_declaration> → "compound" <identifier> "{" <compound_field_list> "}"

<compound_field_list> → <compound_field> { "," <compound_field> } [ "," ]

<compound_field> → "formula" "=" <formula_literal>
                 | "name"    "=" <string_literal>

(* Semantic requirements:
   - The compound body must contain formula and name exactly once.
   - Every element symbol inside <formula_literal> must refer to a declared
     or built-in element. *)

(* ============================================================
   9. Reaction Declarations
   ============================================================ *)

<reaction_declaration> → "reaction" <identifier> "{" <reaction_field_list> "}"

<reaction_field_list> → <reaction_field> { "," <reaction_field> } [ "," ]

<reaction_field> → "reactants" "=" <reaction_expression>
                 | "products"  "=" <reaction_expression>
                 | "check"     "=" <balance_check>
                 | "energy"    "=" <energy_expression>

<balance_check> → "balanced"

<energy_expression> → <energy_kind> <quantity_literal>

<energy_kind> → "exothermic" | "endothermic"

(* Semantic requirements:
   - The reaction body must contain reactants, products, check, and energy
     exactly once.
   - If check = balanced appears, the semantic checker verifies equal atom
     counts on both sides.
   - exothermic stores a negative delta-energy; endothermic stores positive. *)

(* ============================================================
   10. Reaction Expressions
   ============================================================ *)

<reaction_expression> → <reaction_term> { "+" <reaction_term> }

<reaction_term> → <species_ref>
                | <coefficient> "*" <species_ref>

<coefficient> → <number_literal>

<species_ref> → <formula_literal> | <identifier>

(* Examples accepted:
       CH4 + 2*O2        CO2 + 2*H2O
       methane + 2*oxygen    co2 + 2*water

   In reaction context + separates species and * attaches a coefficient, so
   CH4 + 2*O2 parses as CH4 + (2*O2), not (CH4 + 2) * O2.
   ANS requires 2*O2 rather than 2O2 to avoid ambiguity with formula subscripts. *)

(* ============================================================
   11. Expressions
   ============================================================ *)

<expression> → <comparison_expression>

<comparison_expression> → <additive_expression>
                          [ ( "==" | "!=" | ">=" | "<=" | ">" | "<" )
                            <additive_expression> ]

<additive_expression> → <multiplicative_expression>
                        { ( "+" | "-" ) <multiplicative_expression> }

<multiplicative_expression> → <unary_expression>
                               { ( "*" | "/" ) <unary_expression> }

<unary_expression> → [ "-" ] <postfix_expression>

<postfix_expression> → <primary_expression> { <postfix_operator> }

<postfix_operator> → "." <identifier>
                   | "[" <expression> "]"
                   | "(" [ <argument_list> ] ")"

<primary_expression> → <number_or_quantity_literal>
                     | <string_literal>
                     | <char_literal>
                     | <list_literal>
                     | <formula_literal>
                     | <identifier>
                     | "(" <expression> ")"

<argument_list> → <expression> { "," <expression> }

<number_or_quantity_literal> → <number_literal> [ <unit_literal> ]

<quantity_literal> → <number_literal> <unit_literal>

<list_literal> → "[" [ <argument_list> ] "]"

(* Operator precedence (lowest to highest):
   1. comparison:     == != >= <= > <
   2. additive:       + -
   3. multiplicative: * /
   4. unary:          -
   5. postfix:        call ( ), index [ ], property .
   6. primary:        literals, identifiers, ( <expression> )
   Binary +, -, *, / are left-associative (left-to-right repetition in grammar). *)

(* ============================================================
   12. Assignable Expressions
   ============================================================ *)

<assignable> → <identifier> { <assignable_postfix> }

<assignable_postfix> → "." <identifier>
                     | "[" <expression> "]"

(* Function-call syntax is excluded from <assignable>, so f(x) = 3 is invalid. *)

(* ============================================================
   13. Lexical Nonterminals
   ============================================================ *)

<identifier>      → IDENTIFIER
<number_literal>  → NUMBER_LITERAL
<string_literal>  → STRING_LITERAL
<char_literal>    → CHAR_LITERAL
<formula_literal> → FORMULA_LITERAL
<unit_literal>    → UNIT_LITERAL

(* Lexer patterns:

   IDENTIFIER:
       [a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*

   NUMBER_LITERAL:
       (?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?

   STRING_LITERAL:
       "(?:[^"\\\r\n]|\\["\\nrt])*"

   CHAR_LITERAL:
       '(?:[^'\\\r\n]|\\['\\nrt])'

   FORMULA_LITERAL:
       (?:[A-Z][a-z]?(?:[1-9][0-9]*)?)+

   UNIT_LITERAL:
       (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:kg/mol|g/mol|kJ/mol|mol|kg|g|kJ)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])

   OPERATOR:
       ==|!=|>=|<=|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|=|[+\-*/><]

   SEPARATOR:
       [{}()\[\],;.]

   COMMENT:
       //[^\r\n]*

   WHITESPACE:
       [ \t\f\r\n]+
*)

(* ============================================================
   14. Contextual Keyword and Unit Resolution
   ============================================================ *)

(* Hard reserved words:
     let  function  return  for  in  if  elif  else  print  import

   Contextual declaration/chemistry words:
     element  compound  reaction  atomic_mass  valence  symbol  formula
     name  reactants  products  check  balanced  energy  exothermic  endothermic

   Contextual unit words:
     mol  g  kg  g/mol  kg/mol  kJ  kJ/mol

   Resolution rules:
   - At declaration start, element/compound/reaction are declaration keywords.
   - Inside declaration bodies, field-name words are field identifiers.
   - Immediately before an <identifier> inside <parameter_list>, element,
     compound, and reaction are parsed as <type_name> annotations.
   - In expression and property positions the same words are identifiers.
   - A unit literal is recognised only when it directly follows a number (5.0 mol).
   - Elsewhere mol and similar words are plain identifiers. *)

(* ============================================================
   15. Ambiguity Summary
   ============================================================ *)

(*
1. Operator precedence:
   Resolved by separate comparison, additive, multiplicative, unary, postfix,
   and primary expression levels.

2. Reaction precedence:
   Resolved by a separate <reaction_expression> grammar.

3. Stoichiometric coefficient ambiguity:
   Resolved by requiring 2*O2 instead of 2O2.

4. Formula versus identifier ambiguity:
   Identifiers start with a lowercase letter or _; formula literals start with

5. Compound-name species versus formula species:

9. Function call versus assignable expression:
   Function calls are valid expressions but not valid assignment targets.

10. Duplicate declaration fields:
    Field duplication and missing required fields are semantic errors.
*)

1	"""
2	Bookstore Inventory Management System
3	=====================================
4	A demonstration of various Python syntax features:
5	- Type hints, dataclasses, enums
6	- Classes, inheritance, properties
7	- Decorators, generators, lambdas
8	- Comprehensions (list, dict, set, generator)
9	- Exception handling
10	- f-strings, walrus operator, tuple unpacking
11	"""
12	
13	import json
14	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
15	from datetime import datetime
16	from enum import Enum
17	from typing import Optional
18	
19	
20	# ---------- Enum ----------
21	class Genre(Enum):
22	    FICTION = "Fiction"
23	    NON_FICTION = "Non-Fiction"
24	    SCIENCE = "Science"
25	    HISTORY = "History"
26	    BIOGRAPHY = "Biography"
27	
28	
29	# ---------- Dataclass with type hints ----------
30	@dataclass
31	class Book:
32	    title: str
33	    author: str
34	    genre: Genre
35	    price: float
36	    stock: int = 0
37	    isbn: Optional[str] = None
38	    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
39	
40	    def __str__(self) -> str:
41	        return f"'{self.title}' by {self.author} (${self.price:.2f})"
42	
43	    @property
44	    def is_in_stock(self) -> bool:
45	        return self.stock > 0
46	
47	
48	# ---------- Decorator ----------
49	def log_action(func):
50	    """A decorator that logs function calls with timestamps."""
51	
52	    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
53	        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
54	        print(f"[{timestamp}] -> {func.__name__}()")
55	        return func(*args, **kwargs)
56	
57	    return wrapper
58	
59	
60	# ---------- Main class ----------
61	class Inventory:
62	    def __init__(self, store_name: str):
63	        self.store_name = store_name
64	        self.books: dict[str, Book] = {}
65	        self.sales_history: list[dict] = []
66	
67	    @log_action
68	    def add_book(self, book: Book, quantity: int = 1) -> None:
69	        if book.title in self.books:
70	            self.books[book.title].stock += quantity
71	        else:
72	            book.stock = quantity
73	            self.books[book.title] = book
74	        print(f"   Added {quantity}x {book}")
75	
76	    @log_action
77	    def sell_book(self, title: str, quantity: int = 1) -> float:
78	        if title not in self.books:
79	            raise ValueError(f"Book '{title}' not found in inventory")
80	
81	        book = self.books[title]
82	        if book.stock < quantity:
83	            raise ValueError(f"Only {book.stock} copies of '{title}' available")
84	
85	        book.stock -= quantity
86	        total = book.price * quantity
87	
88	        self.sales_history.append(
89	            {
90	                "title": title,
91	                "quantity": quantity,
92	                "total": round(total, 2),
93	                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
94	            }
95	        )
96	
97	        print(f"   Sold {quantity}x {book} for ${total:.2f}")
98	        return total
99	
100	    def search_by_genre(self, genre: Genre) -> list[Book]:
101	        # List comprehension with filter
102	        return [book for book in self.books.values() if book.genre == genre]
103	
104	    def get_total_value(self) -> float:
105	        # Generator expression passed to sum()
106	        return sum(book.price * book.stock for book in self.books.values())
107	
108	    def get_low_stock(self, threshold: int = 3) -> list[Book]:
109	        return [b for b in self.books.values() if 0 < b.stock <= threshold]
110	
111	
112	# ---------- Generator function ----------
113	def fibonacci(n: int):
114	    """Yield the first n Fibonacci numbers."""
115	    a, b = 0, 1
116	    for _ in range(n):
117	        yield a
118	        a, b = b, a + b
119	
120	
121	# ---------- Lambda + higher-order function ----------
122	def apply_discount(books: list[Book], discount: float) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
123	    discount_fn = lambda price: price * (1 - discount)
124	    return [(book.title, round(discount_fn(book.price), 2)) for book in books]
125	
126	
127	def main():
128	    print("=" * 55)
129	    print("       BOOKSTORE INVENTORY DEMO")
130	    print("=" * 55)
131	
132	    store = Inventory("The Reading Corner")
133	
134	    # Sample data
135	    sample_books = [
136	        Book(
137	            "The Great Gatsby",
138	            "F. Scott Fitzgerald",
139	            Genre.FICTION,
140	            12.99,
141	            isbn="978-0743273565",
142	        ),
143	        Book(
144	            "Sapiens",
145	            "Yuval Noah Harari",
146	            Genre.HISTORY,
147	            18.50,
148	            tags=["bestseller", "anthropology"],
149	        ),
150	        Book("A Brief History of Time", "Stephen Hawking", Genre.SCIENCE, 15.00),
151	        Book(
152	            "1984", "George Orwell", Genre.FICTION, 10.99, tags=["classic", "dystopia"]
153	        ),
154	        Book("Steve Jobs", "Walter Isaacson", Genre.BIOGRAPHY, 22.00),
155	    ]
156	
157	    # Loop through and add stock
158	    print("\n--- STOCKING THE STORE ---")
159	    for book in sample_books:
160	        store.add_book(book, quantity=5)
161	
162	    print(f"\nTotal inventory value: ${store.get_total_value():.2f}")
163	
164	    # Exception handling
165	    print("\n--- SALES ---")
166	    for title, qty in [("1984", 2), ("Sapiens", 3), ("Unknown Book", 1), ("1984", 99)]:
167	        try:
168	            store.sell_book(title, qty)
169	        except ValueError as e:
170	            print(f"   ! Error: {e}")
171	
172	    # Search and conditional expression
173	    print("\n--- FICTION BOOKS ---")
174	    for book in store.search_by_genre(Genre.FICTION):
175	        status = "in stock" if book.is_in_stock else "out of stock"
176	        print(f"   {book} - {status} ({book.stock} left)")
177	
178	    # Set comprehension
179	    all_authors = {book.author for book in store.books.values()}
180	    print(f"\nUnique authors: {len(all_authors)}")
181	
182	    # Tuple unpacking with star expression
183	    first, *middle, last = "Yuval Noah Harari".split()
184	    print(f"First: {first}, Middle: {middle}, Last: {last}")
185	
186	    # Lambda usage
187	    print("\n--- 20% OFF FICTION ---")
188	    for title, new_price in apply_discount(store.search_by_genre(Genre.FICTION), 0.20):
189	        print(f"   {title}: ${new_price}")
190	
191	    # Generator
192	    print("\n--- FIBONACCI (first 10) ---")
193	    print(f"   {list(fibonacci(10))}")
194	
195	    # f-string formatting tricks
196	    pi = 3.14159265359
197	    print(f"\nPi: {pi:.4f} | Percent: {0.875:.2%} | Hex of 255: {255:#x}")
198	
199	    # Walrus operator (Python 3.8+)
200	    if (n := len(store.books)) > 3:
201	        print(f"\nLarge inventory detected: {n} unique titles")
202	
203	    # Dict comprehension
204	    stock_map = {book.title: book.stock for book in store.books.values()}
205	    print(f"\nStock map: {stock_map}")
206	
207	    # JSON serialization
208	    print("\n--- SALES HISTORY (JSON) ---")
209	    print(json.dumps(store.sales_history, indent=2))

"""

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
from typing import Optional


# ---------- Enum ----------
class Genre(Enum):
    FICTION = "Fiction"
    NON_FICTION = "Non-Fiction"
    SCIENCE = "Science"
    HISTORY = "History"
    BIOGRAPHY = "Biography"


# ---------- Dataclass with type hints ----------
@dataclass
class Book:
    title: str
    author: str
    genre: Genre
    price: float
    stock: int = 0
    isbn: Optional[str] = None
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"'{self.title}' by {self.author} (${self.price:.2f})"

    @property
    def is_in_stock(self) -> bool:
        return self.stock > 0


# ---------- Decorator ----------
def log_action(func):
    """A decorator that logs function calls with timestamps."""

    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        print(f"[{timestamp}] -> {func.__name__}()")
        return func(*args, **kwargs)

    return wrapper


# ---------- Main class ----------
class Inventory:
    def __init__(self, store_name: str):
        self.store_name = store_name
        self.books: dict[str, Book] = {}
        self.sales_history: list[dict] = []

    @log_action
    def add_book(self, book: Book, quantity: int = 1) -> None:
        if book.title in self.books:
            self.books[book.title].stock += quantity
        else:
            book.stock = quantity
            self.books[book.title] = book
        print(f"   Added {quantity}x {book}")

    @log_action
    def sell_book(self, title: str, quantity: int = 1) -> float:
        if title not in self.books:
            raise ValueError(f"Book '{title}' not found in inventory")

        book = self.books[title]
        if book.stock < quantity:
            raise ValueError(f"Only {book.stock} copies of '{title}' available")

        book.stock -= quantity
        total = book.price * quantity

        self.sales_history.append(
            {
                "title": title,
                "quantity": quantity,
                "total": round(total, 2),
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
            }
        )

        print(f"   Sold {quantity}x {book} for ${total:.2f}")
        return total

    def search_by_genre(self, genre: Genre) -> list[Book]:
        # List comprehension with filter
        return [book for book in self.books.values() if book.genre == genre]

    def get_total_value(self) -> float:
        # Generator expression passed to sum()
        return sum(book.price * book.stock for book in self.books.values())

    def get_low_stock(self, threshold: int = 3) -> list[Book]:
        return [b for b in self.books.values() if 0 < b.stock <= threshold]


# ---------- Generator function ----------
def fibonacci(n: int):
    """Yield the first n Fibonacci numbers."""
    a, b = 0, 1
    for _ in range(n):
        yield a
        a, b = b, a + b


# ---------- Lambda + higher-order function ----------
def apply_discount(books: list[Book], discount: float) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    discount_fn = lambda price: price * (1 - discount)
    return [(book.title, round(discount_fn(book.price), 2)) for book in books]


def main():
    print("=" * 55)
    print("       BOOKSTORE INVENTORY DEMO")
    print("=" * 55)

    store = Inventory("The Reading Corner")

    # Sample data
    sample_books = [
        Book(
            "The Great Gatsby",
            "F. Scott Fitzgerald",
            Genre.FICTION,
            12.99,
            isbn="978-0743273565",
        ),
        Book(
            "Sapiens",
            "Yuval Noah Harari",
            Genre.HISTORY,
            18.50,
            tags=["bestseller", "anthropology"],
        ),
        Book("A Brief History of Time", "Stephen Hawking", Genre.SCIENCE, 15.00),
        Book(
            "1984", "George Orwell", Genre.FICTION, 10.99, tags=["classic", "dystopia"]
        ),
        Book("Steve Jobs", "Walter Isaacson", Genre.BIOGRAPHY, 22.00),
    ]

    # Loop through and add stock
    print("\n--- STOCKING THE STORE ---")
    for book in sample_books:
        store.add_book(book, quantity=5)

    print(f"\nTotal inventory value: ${store.get_total_value():.2f}")

    # Exception handling
    print("\n--- SALES ---")
    for title, qty in [("1984", 2), ("Sapiens", 3), ("Unknown Book", 1), ("1984", 99)]:
        try:
            store.sell_book(title, qty)
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"   ! Error: {e}")

    # Search and conditional expression
    print("\n--- FICTION BOOKS ---")
    for book in store.search_by_genre(Genre.FICTION):
        status = "in stock" if book.is_in_stock else "out of stock"
        print(f"   {book} - {status} ({book.stock} left)")

    # Set comprehension
    all_authors = {book.author for book in store.books.values()}
    print(f"\nUnique authors: {len(all_authors)}")

    # Tuple unpacking with star expression
    first, *middle, last = "Yuval Noah Harari".split()
    print(f"First: {first}, Middle: {middle}, Last: {last}")

    # Lambda usage
    print("\n--- 20% OFF FICTION ---")
    for title, new_price in apply_discount(store.search_by_genre(Genre.FICTION), 0.20):
        print(f"   {title}: ${new_price}")

    # Generator
    print("\n--- FIBONACCI (first 10) ---")
    print(f"   {list(fibonacci(10))}")

    # f-string formatting tricks
    pi = 3.14159265359
    print(f"\nPi: {pi:.4f} | Percent: {0.875:.2%} | Hex of 255: {255:#x}")

    # Walrus operator (Python 3.8+)
    if (n := len(store.books)) > 3:
        print(f"\nLarge inventory detected: {n} unique titles")

    # Dict comprehension
    stock_map = {book.title: book.stock for book in store.books.values()}
    print(f"\nStock map: {stock_map}")

    # JSON serialization
    print("\n--- SALES HISTORY (JSON) ---")
    print(json.dumps(store.sales_history, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	(*
2	ANS Complete EBNF Grammar
3	Sebesta-style notation for the implemented C-like ANS subset.
4	
5	Conventions:
6	  <nonterminal> → production
7	  terminal      means exact source text (shown in lowercase or quoted)
8	  { X }         means zero or more repetitions of X
9	  [ X ]         means optional X
10	  ( X | Y )     means one of the alternatives X or Y
11	  |             separates top-level alternatives in a rule
12	  EOF           means end of file
13	
14	Important lexer convention:
15	  ANS uses contextual chemistry words. Lowercase words are first tokenized
16	  as IDENTIFIER-like words. The parser interprets words such as element,
17	  compound, reaction, formula, reactants, products, balanced, exothermic,
18	  and endothermic as special words only in grammar positions where they
19	  have special meaning. This allows typed parameters such as:
20	
21	      function compute_yield(reaction r, compound c) { ... };
22	      function molar_mass(compound c) { ... };
23	*)
24	
25	(* ============================================================
26	   1. Program Structure
27	   ============================================================ *)
28	
29	<program> → { <top_level_statement> } EOF
30	
31	<top_level_statement> → <import_statement> ";"
32	                      | <element_declaration> ";"
33	                      | <compound_declaration> ";"
34	                      | <reaction_declaration> ";"
35	                      | <function_declaration> ";"
36	                      | <variable_declaration> ";"
37	                      | <assignment_statement> ";"
38	                      | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
39	                      | <print_statement> ";"
40	                      | <expression_statement> ";"
41	                      | <if_statement>
42	
43	(* ============================================================
44	   2. Import Statements
45	   ============================================================ *)
46	
47	<import_statement> → "import" <identifier>
48	
49	(* Examples accepted:
50	       import std
51	
52	   Semantic requirement: the named module must exist in the ANS standard library
53	   or the local module path. Import resolution is a semantic phase concern. *)
54	
55	(* ============================================================
56	   3. General Statements and Blocks
57	   ============================================================ *)
58	
59	<block> → "{" { <statement> } "}"
60	
61	<statement> → <variable_declaration> ";"
62	            | <assignment_statement> ";"
63	            | <augmented_assignment_statement> ";"
64	            | <return_statement> ";"
65	            | <print_statement> ";"
66	            | <expression_statement> ";"
67	            | <for_statement>
68	            | <if_statement>
69	
70	<variable_declaration> → "let" <identifier> "=" <expression>
71	
72	<assignment_statement> → <assignable> "=" <expression>
73	
74	<augmented_assignment_statement> → <assignable> <augmented_assignment_operator> <expression>
75	
76	<augmented_assignment_operator> → "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/="
77	
78	<return_statement> → "return" [ <expression> ]
79	
80	<print_statement> → "print" <expression>
81	
82	<expression_statement> → <expression>
83	
84	(* ============================================================
85	   4. Function Declarations
86	   ============================================================ *)
87	
88	<function_declaration> → "function" <identifier> "(" [ <parameter_list> ] ")" <block>
89	
90	<parameter_list> → <parameter> { "," <parameter> }
91	
92	<parameter> → [ <type_name> ] <identifier>
93	
94	<type_name> → "element" | "compound" | "reaction"
95	
96	(* Typed parameters allow the type-checker to verify that the correct kind of
97	   value is passed at call sites. The type annotation is optional; untyped
98	   parameters accept any value. Examples:
99	       reaction r    compound c    element e    mol (untyped)
100	
101	   Ambiguity resolution:
102	   element, compound, and reaction are parsed as <type_name> only when they
103	   immediately precede an <identifier> inside a <parameter_list>. Elsewhere
104	   these words may still appear as identifiers. *)
105	
106	(* ============================================================
107	   5. For Loops
108	   ============================================================ *)
109	
110	<for_statement> → "for" "(" "let" <identifier> "in" <expression> ")" <block>
111	
112	(* Example:
113	   for (let element in formula) {
114	       mass += element.atomic_mass * formula[element];
115	   }
116	*)
117	
118	(* ============================================================
119	   6. If / Elif / Else Statements
120	   ============================================================ *)
121	
122	<if_statement> → "if" "(" <expression> ")" <block>
123	                 { <elif_clause> } [ <else_clause> ]
124	
125	<elif_clause> → "elif" "(" <expression> ")" <block>
126	
127	<else_clause> → "else" <block>
128	
129	(* Conditions are always wrapped in parentheses, matching the for-loop style.
130	
131	   Dangling-else resolution:
132	   Every branch body is a braced <block>, so the classic unbraced ambiguity
133	       if a if b s else t
134	   cannot arise. The optional <else_clause> belongs to the nearest preceding
135	   <if_statement>. *)
136	
137	(* ============================================================
138	   7. Element Declarations
139	   ============================================================ *)
140	
141	<element_declaration> → "element" <element_symbol> "{" <element_field_list> "}"
142	
143	<element_symbol> → <formula_literal>
144	
145	<element_field_list> → <element_field> { "," <element_field> } [ "," ]
146	
147	<element_field> → "atomic_mass" "=" <number_literal>
148	                | "valence"     "=" <number_literal>
149	                | "symbol"      "=" <string_literal>
150	
151	(* Semantic requirements:
152	   - <element_symbol> must be a single valid periodic-table symbol (e.g., H).
153	   - The element body must contain atomic_mass, valence, and symbol exactly once.
154	   - Duplicate or missing fields are semantic errors, not syntax errors.
155	   H is lexically a <formula_literal>; after "element" it is an element symbol. *)
156	
157	(* ============================================================
158	   8. Compound Declarations
159	   ============================================================ *)
160	
161	<compound_declaration> → "compound" <identifier> "{" <compound_field_list> "}"
162	
163	<compound_field_list> → <compound_field> { "," <compound_field> } [ "," ]
164	
165	<compound_field> → "formula" "=" <formula_literal>
166	                 | "name"    "=" <string_literal>
167	
168	(* Semantic requirements:
169	   - The compound body must contain formula and name exactly once.
170	   - Every element symbol inside <formula_literal> must refer to a declared
171	     or built-in element. *)
172	
173	(* ============================================================
174	   9. Reaction Declarations
175	   ============================================================ *)
176	
177	<reaction_declaration> → "reaction" <identifier> "{" <reaction_field_list> "}"
178	
179	<reaction_field_list> → <reaction_field> { "," <reaction_field> } [ "," ]
180	
181	<reaction_field> → "reactants" "=" <reaction_expression>
182	                 | "products"  "=" <reaction_expression>
183	                 | "check"     "=" <balance_check>
184	                 | "energy"    "=" <energy_expression>
185	
186	<balance_check> → "balanced"
187	
188	<energy_expression> → <energy_kind> <quantity_literal>
189	
190	<energy_kind> → "exothermic" | "endothermic"
191	
192	(* Semantic requirements:
193	   - The reaction body must contain reactants, products, check, and energy
194	     exactly once.
195	   - If check = balanced appears, the semantic checker verifies equal atom
196	     counts on both sides.
197	   - exothermic stores a negative delta-energy; endothermic stores positive. *)
198	
199	(* ============================================================
200	   10. Reaction Expressions
201	   ============================================================ *)
202	
203	<reaction_expression> → <reaction_term> { "+" <reaction_term> }
204	
205	<reaction_term> → <species_ref>
206	                | <coefficient> "*" <species_ref>
207	
208	<coefficient> → <number_literal>
209	
210	<species_ref> → <formula_literal> | <identifier>
211	
212	(* Examples accepted:
213	       CH4 + 2*O2        CO2 + 2*H2O
214	       methane + 2*oxygen    co2 + 2*water
215	
216	   In reaction context + separates species and * attaches a coefficient, so
217	   CH4 + 2*O2 parses as CH4 + (2*O2), not (CH4 + 2) * O2.
218	   ANS requires 2*O2 rather than 2O2 to avoid ambiguity with formula subscripts. *)
219	
220	(* ============================================================
221	   11. Expressions
222	   ============================================================ *)
223	
224	<expression> → <comparison_expression>
225	
226	<comparison_expression> → <additive_expression>
227	                          [ ( "==" | "!=" | ">=" | "<=" | ">" | "<" )
228	                            <additive_expression> ]
229	
230	<additive_expression> → <multiplicative_expression>
231	                        { ( "+" | "-" ) <multiplicative_expression> }
232	
233	<multiplicative_expression> → <unary_expression>
234	                               { ( "*" | "/" ) <unary_expression> }
235	
236	<unary_expression> → [ "-" ] <postfix_expression>
237	
238	<postfix_expression> → <primary_expression> { <postfix_operator> }
239	
240	<postfix_operator> → "." <identifier>
241	                   | "[" <expression> "]"
242	                   | "(" [ <argument_list> ] ")"
243	
244	<primary_expression> → <number_or_quantity_literal>
245	                     | <string_literal>
246	                     | <char_literal>
247	                     | <list_literal>
248	                     | <formula_literal>
249	                     | <identifier>
250	                     | "(" <expression> ")"
251	
252	<argument_list> → <expression> { "," <expression> }
253	
254	<number_or_quantity_literal> → <number_literal> [ <unit_literal> ]
255	
256	<quantity_literal> → <number_literal> <unit_literal>
257	
258	<list_literal> → "[" [ <argument_list> ] "]"
259	
260	(* Operator precedence (lowest to highest):
261	   1. comparison:     == != >= <= > <
262	   2. additive:       + -
263	   3. multiplicative: * /
264	   4. unary:          -
265	   5. postfix:        call ( ), index [ ], property .
266	   6. primary:        literals, identifiers, ( <expression> )
267	   Binary +, -, *, / are left-associative (left-to-right repetition in grammar). *)
268	
269	(* ============================================================
270	   12. Assignable Expressions
271	   ============================================================ *)
272	
273	<assignable> → <identifier> { <assignable_postfix> }
274	
275	<assignable_postfix> → "." <identifier>
276	                     | "[" <expression> "]"
277	
278	(* Function-call syntax is excluded from <assignable>, so f(x) = 3 is invalid. *)
279	
280	(* ============================================================
281	   13. Lexical Nonterminals
282	   ============================================================ *)
283	
284	<identifier>      → IDENTIFIER
285	<number_literal>  → NUMBER_LITERAL
286	<string_literal>  → STRING_LITERAL
287	<char_literal>    → CHAR_LITERAL
288	<formula_literal> → FORMULA_LITERAL
289	<unit_literal>    → UNIT_LITERAL
290	
291	(* Lexer patterns:
292	
293	   IDENTIFIER:
294	       [a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
295	
296	   NUMBER_LITERAL:
297	       (?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?
298	
299	   STRING_LITERAL:
300	       "(?:[^"\\\r\n]|\\["\\nrt])*"
301	
302	   CHAR_LITERAL:
303	       '(?:[^'\\\r\n]|\\['\\nrt])'
304	
305	   FORMULA_LITERAL:
306	       (?:[A-Z][a-z]?(?:[1-9][0-9]*)?)+
307	
308	   UNIT_LITERAL:
309	       (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:kg/mol|g/mol|kJ/mol|mol|kg|g|kJ)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])
310	
311	   OPERATOR:
312	       ==|!=|>=|<=|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|=|[+\-*/><]
313	
314	   SEPARATOR:
315	       [{}()\[\],;.]
316	
317	   COMMENT:
318	       //[^\r\n]*
319	
320	   WHITESPACE:
321	       [ \t\f\r\n]+
322	*)
323	
324	(* ============================================================
325	   14. Contextual Keyword and Unit Resolution
326	   ============================================================ *)
327	
328	(* Hard reserved words:
329	     let  function  return  for  in  if  elif  else  print  import
330	
331	   Contextual declaration/chemistry words:
332	     element  compound  reaction  atomic_mass  valence  symbol  formula
333	     name  reactants  products  check  balanced  energy  exothermic  endothermic
334	
335	   Contextual unit words:
336	     mol  g  kg  g/mol  kg/mol  kJ  kJ/mol
337	
338	   Resolution rules:
339	   - At declaration start, element/compound/reaction are declaration keywords.
340	   - Inside declaration bodies, field-name words are field identifiers.
341	   - Immediately before an <identifier> inside <parameter_list>, element,
342	     compound, and reaction are parsed as <type_name> annotations.
343	   - In expression and property positions the same words are identifiers.
344	   - A unit literal is recognised only when it directly follows a number (5.0 mol).
345	   - Elsewhere mol and similar words are plain identifiers. *)
346	
347	(* ============================================================
348	   15. Ambiguity Summary
349	   ============================================================ *)
350	
351	(*
352	1. Operator precedence:
353	   Resolved by separate comparison, additive, multiplicative, unary, postfix,
354	   and primary expression levels.
355	
356	2. Reaction precedence:
357	   Resolved by a separate <reaction_expression> grammar.
358	
359	3. Stoichiometric coefficient ambiguity:
360	   Resolved by requiring 2*O2 instead of 2O2.
361	
362	4. Formula versus identifier ambiguity:
363	   Identifiers start with a lowercase letter or _; formula literals start with
364	   an uppercase letter. water is an identifier; H2O is a formula literal.
365	
366	5. Compound-name species versus formula species:
367	   Resolved by <species_ref>, which accepts either form inside reactions.
368	
369	6. Keyword versus identifier ambiguity:
370	   Resolved with contextual keywords. element, compound, and reaction act as
371	   type annotations in parameter lists; everywhere else they are identifiers.
372	
373	7. Unit versus identifier ambiguity:
374	   Resolved contextually: mol is a unit after a number, an identifier elsewhere.
375	
376	8. Dangling else:
377	   Avoided by requiring braced <block> bodies; else attaches to the nearest if.
378	
379	9. Function call versus assignable expression:
380	   Function calls are valid expressions but not valid assignment targets.
381	
382	10. Duplicate declaration fields:
383	    Field duplication and missing required fields are semantic errors.
384	*)
385
